svg.title: From Chance Mould to Allied Miracle Drug: Scaling Penicillin (1928–1944)
svg.desc: Three-column comparative engineering and historical factor diagram of penicillin: 1. 1928 Discovery by Alexander Fleming at St Mary's Hospital (Penicillium notatum killing Staphylococci on an agar plate, unstable and unpurified), 2. 1938-41 Oxford Purification by Howard Florey, Ernst Chain and Norman Heatley (ceramic bedpans, milk churns, 1940 8-mice trial, Constable Albert Alexander dying when tiny supply ran out despite recycling from urine), and 3. 1941-44 US Industrial Scale-Up (US War Production Board, Peoria cantaloupe strain and corn-steep liquor, Pfizer 10,000-gallon aerated deep-fermentation tanks producing 2.3 million doses for D-Day June 1944).
svg.text: EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY · FIRST TRUE ANTIBIOTIC & INDUSTRIAL MEDICINE (1928–1945)
From Chance Mould to Allied Miracle Drug: Scaling Penicillin (1928–1944)
Alexander Fleming · St Mary's Hospital, London
deadly Staphylococci on an unwashed dish.
but it was chemically unstable & impure.
Fleming moved on — zero systemic cures.
Howard Florey, Ernst Chain & Norman Heatley
died when tiny supply ran out
dried pure penicillin from Fleming's paper.
across hundreds of ceramic bedpans, milk
• Wartime UK Limit: Blitz bombing & munitions
left British chemical firms unable to scale;
Florey & Heatley flew to the USA (July 1941)
with mould spores smeared in their coat linings.
~2,000 Litres of Fluid Needed for 1 Patient
US War Production Board · Peoria Lab · Pfizer
• US Government Backing: After Pearl Harbor,
the US War Production Board funded 21
tanks pumping sterile air through broth.
• Allied Miracle Drug: 2.3 million doses ready
civilian NHS antibiotic era followed post-1945.
EDEXCEL 16-MARK EVALUATION · WHY INDIVIDUAL GENIUS ALONE DID NOT CREATE MASS ANTIBIOTICS
1. Chance & Observation (Fleming, 1928) spotted the mould → 2. Science & Teamwork (Florey, Chain & Heatley, 1938–41) proved clinical
cure → 3. War, US Government Finance & Chemical Industry (1941–44) solved mass engineering so penicillin saved millions of lives.
